descriptor: Serial-acquirer bio-analytical testing lab network · reported in EUR

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

organicGrowth.title: Organic vs reported revenue growth
organicGrowth.content:
Reported revenue growth includes everything: acquisitions, disposals, currency moves and organic volume/price. Organic growth strips all of that out to show growth from the existing lab network at constant scope and FX.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: Eurofins has done roughly 40 bolt-on acquisitions a year historically, so reported growth routinely runs well ahead of organic growth; management's long-term objective is 6.5% p.a. organic, and delivered organic growth was 7.1% / 4.7% / 4.1% in FY2023-25. The gap between the two bars in a given year is the M&A (and FX) contribution.

What to watch:

  • Organic growth trending toward or away from the 6.5% long-term objective
  • A widening gap to reported growth, which signals heavier reliance on acquired revenue
  • FY2020-22 is distorted by the COVID-testing windfall and its unwind -- not a clean read on the underlying network

adjustedEbitda.title: Adjusted vs reported EBITDA
adjustedEbitda.content:
Reported EBITDA is as filed. Adjusted EBITDA is management's measure that excludes significant non-recurring items (restructuring, litigation, acquisition costs, and in FY2020-22 COVID-testing-related swings).

For Eurofins Scientific SE: as a serial acquirer, Eurofins carries recurring integration and restructuring charges that reported EBITDA absorbs every year; the adjusted figure is management's view of run-rate profitability and is the number guidance targets are set against.

What to watch:

  • A persistently widening gap between adjusted and reported EBITDA (adjustments becoming the norm rather than the exception)
  • Adjusted margin trend versus reported margin

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the growth rate matters more than the level; see the Organic vs Reported Revenue Growth chart below for how much of it is bought via acquisition.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Eurofins Scientific SE: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
